findings.evidence: Mathlib/Algebra/Algebra/Tower.lean:235 defines `AlgEquiv.restrictScalars`; lines 174–190 reconstruct that operation and then prove an `rfl` application lemma plus inherited injectivity.
findings.fix: Use `(integralFieldBaseChangeEquiv L v).restrictScalars (𝒪 K) |>.toAlgHom` directly; use the equivalence’s standard coercion and `.injective`, deleting all three private declarations.
findings.issue: `integralFieldBaseChangeAlgHom`, its `_apply` lemma, and its `_injective` lemma manually repackage `integralFieldBaseChangeEquiv` after restricting scalars.

findings.evidence: Mathlib/Algebra/Algebra/Tower.lean:182 defines `AlgHom.restrictScalars`; lines 192–211 duplicate its tower compatibility proof and then wrap the already suitable `Algebra.TensorProduct.map` solely to repeat `commutes'`.
findings.fix: Replace the former by `(algebraMap (v.adicCompletionIntegers K) (v.adicCompletion K)).restrictScalars (𝒪 K)`, and define the latter directly with `Algebra.TensorProduct.map` on that map and `AlgHom.id`.
findings.issue: `adicCompletionIntegersToCompletion` and the structure literal in `integralTensorToBaseChange` manually rebuild existing restricted algebra maps and tensor-product mapping.

summary: The main construction is new, but its base-change implementation duplicates Mathlib’s scalar-restriction APIs with hand-built wrappers and tautological lemmas.
